correctness.rationale: For every integer \(m\ge3\), the known prime CI ladder-graph ideal gives the exact \(m\times(3m+1)\) Jacobian. A nontrivial row relation either contains a zero row or, by disjoint rail columns and the quadratic equations, forces neighboring rows supported at a common rung. This completely describes singular supports as R and J coordinate strata. Each stratum reduces to a tensor product of prime shorter ladder chain CI rings, proving irreducibility, codimension three and regularity of surviving quadrics. Bézout supplies high-degree \(2^{m-2}\) with multiplicity \(m+3\) and low-degree \(2^{m-3}\) with multiplicity \(4(m-2)\); local eliminations show a rank-four ordinary node generically. The packaged executable rechecked \(m=2,\ldots,6\); its finite range is explicitly not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The projective degree of an equidimensional singular locus is a natural intersection-theoretic invariant intrinsic to the standard graph-edge embedding. The full degree multiset distinguishes two types of codimension-three singular components for arbitrarily long graph chains; neither the generic toric smoothness criterion nor the bare graph CI theorem directly outputs this degree distribution. The nontrivial full component enumeration and proof of remaining quadratic regular sequences give a reusable class computation with plausible relevance to polar/intersection geometry, beyond a single arbitrary numerical case.
